content.title: Recap: Mets beat the Pirates on Opening Day — get the highlights from Citi Field
content.text: Live Blog EndedMar 26, 2026 Join NBC New York for live game and pre-game coverage from Queens and follow along below for the latest happenings. NBC Universal, Inc. The New York Mets start their 2026 season at Citi Field as they take on the Pittsburgh Pirates on Opening Day. NBC New York’s Gaby Acevedo reports. The New York Mets started their 2026 season at Citi Field as they take on the Pittsburgh Pirates on Opening Day. Juan Soto and Francisco Lindor are back, along with new acquisitions Bo Bichette and Marcus Semien, as the Amazins look to shake off last season's disappointments and bring the Mets back to the playoffs. NBC New York had live game and pre-game coverage from Queens; see all the happenings below: The 2026 Major League Baseball season kicks off with Opening Day on Thursday, with none other than the New York Mets taking on the Pittsburgh Pirates at Citi Field. First pitch is slated for 1:15 p.m. The game will be on NBC New York on air and streaming on Peacock. And don't forget to tune to News 4 on air or wherever you stream starting at 12 p.m. for a special pregame show with Bruce Beck, John Chandler and more. Mets rookie Carson Benge talks about his performance in an 11-7 win over the Pirates. Freddy Peralta wasn't perfect, but fortunately for him, he didn't need to be. The offense carried the Mets to a 11-7 win over the Pirates on Opening Day. The Amazins used a big first inning to chase from the game Paul Skenes early, as the reigning NL Cy Young winner only made it through two-thirds of a inning, giving up five runs. Peralta struggled to get through five, then Tobias Myers gave them three innings of one-run ball to limit the damage and save the bullpen. Luis Garcia made things a little more interesting in the 9th, giving up two runs on three hits, and giving Pittsburgh a sliver of late hope. But the right-hander was able to shut down any rally attempt, sealing the win for the Mets. Mets catcher Francisco Alvarez hit a solo shot inthe 6th inning against the Pirates. The Mets offense looks like it will carry them to a win on Opening Day. Just moments after Carson Benge had his first career hit go for a home run, catcher Francisco Alvarez added a dinger to left, going more than 420 feet. Mets lead 11-5. Mets rookie Carson Benge hit his first Major League home run on Opening Day. Carson Benge used a spectacular Spring Training to earn a spot on the Mets Opening Day roster, and in the starting lineup. Now he's made a splash in the bigs. After going 0-2 with a walk in his first three at bats, Benge smoked one to right center for his first major league home run — his first hit, too. The home run extended the Mets lead to 10-5. It wasn't the kind of debut he (or fans) might have wanted, but Freddy Peralta battled to get through five innings against the Pirates. The right hander, acquired from Milwaukee in the offseason, gave up four runs on six hits while striking out seven. Thanks to the offense's explosive and surprising first inning against Skenes, Peralta is still in line for a win if the score holds. Luis Robert Jr., who was also added over the offseason but to less fanfare than some of the other acquisitions, contributed in his first game in Flushing. The centerfielder hit a hard groundball through the gap between third and short, driving in a run to extend the Mets' lead to 6-3. @nbcnewyork Twenty-two of the 30 teams will be playing on Thursday for Opening Day. The aforementioned Yankees and Giants kick things off Wednesday, then there’s a trio of series that don’t begin until Friday (Athletics at Toronto Blue Jays, Colorado Rockies at Miami Marlins and Kansas City Royals at Atlanta Braves). Every other team will be in action Thursday. #openingday #mlb #yankees #mets ♬ original sound - NBC New York The MTA shared a few fun stats regarding how people got to Thursday's game: 32,500 people rode the 7 train to Citi Field 6,200 took LIRR to the stadium 2,000 took the "nostalgia" 7 train For reference, Citi Field has a capacity of just under 42,000 — so the vast majority took some form of train to the game. If it weren't for Brandon Lowe, Freddy Peralta's first start as a member of the Mets would be going much better. But as it stands, Peralta has given up three runs, all of which have come via home runs by Lowe. The Pirates' offseason acquisition saw two pitches in his first two at-bats, sending them both over the wall. The Mets challenged a ball four call with the new ABS system. The Mets challenged a ball four call on a 3-2 pitch to Oneil Cruz, and in the process became the first MLB team to win an ABS challenge. The call was quickly overturned, and Cruz went from walking to first base to walking back to the dugout. This is not what many would have seen coming from the defending NL Cy Young Award winner. Paul Skenes was pulled after getting through just two-thirds of an inning. He threw 37 pitches and gave up five runs, in part thanks to some shaky defense from Oneil Cruz in centerfield. Yohan Ramirez came in in relief and retired the side. After misplaying Brett Baty's hard line drive to deep center, Cruz then lost a routine fly ball off the bat of Marcus Semien in the sun. The ball dropped to his left, giving the Mets a 5-2 lead. Brett Baty's bases loaded triple put the Mets up 4-2 in the first inning. Most teams last year would be happy to get a run or two against Paul Skenes. The Mets did that and then some before even recording their second out. With the bases loaded, Brett Baty hit a hard line drive that went over the head of center fielder Oneil Cruz, who appeared to initially come in on the ball. All three runners came around to score, and Baty ended up at third with a 3-RBI triple. Mets lead, 4-2. Bo Bichette hit a sacrafice fly to drive in a run in his first at bat as a New York Met. It didn't take long for Bo Bichette to display his ability to drive in runs. With runners on first and third and no outs, Bichette hit an 0-2 pitch to right for a sacrifice fly in his first at-bat with his new team, cutting the Pirates' lead to 2-1. Brandon Lowe hits a two-run home run in the first inning to put the Pirates up 2-0. And just like that, the Mets are already trailing. After an Oneil Cruz soft liner to center field for a leadoff single, one of the Pirates new additions made his mark. Brandon Lowe pulled a ball down the right field line and just out of reach of the leaping Carson Benge for a two-run homer. Given how good Paul Skenes has been for Pittsburgh in his very young career, that could be all the cushion Pittsburgh needs. Howie Rose introduces the 2026 New York Mets at Citi Field on Opening Day. It always feels good to win on Opening Day, but how often do the Mets get their season off on the right foot? Surprisingly often — moreso than any other franchise, it turns out. The Mets are 41-23 on Opening Day, the best mark among all MLB teams. That's especially surprising given that the franchise lost its first eight games on Opening Day, starting with the team's first year in 1962 and inlcuding the 1969 Miracle Mets year. Since 1970, the team is 41-15 on Opening Day. The Mariners have the second-best winning percentage, going 30-19. The Orioles, Yankees and Dodgers round out the top five. The newest member of the New York team brings plenty to the plate. NBC New York's Bruce Beck interviews the third baseman. @nbcnewyork Grab your peanuts and Cracker Jack — first pitch is quickly approaching. After the thrilling World Baseball Classic and weeks of spring training, the MLB season has arrived. While it might not feel like spring in some cities just yet, baseball is a sure sign of the warmer days ahead. #openingday #baseball #mlb ♬ original sound - NBC New York NBC New York's Bruce Beck shares one-on-one interview with Mets' Juan Soto.It's been 40 years since the Mets' last World Series title. NBC New York's John Chandler revisits the legendary team of '86. For Long Island Rail Road commuters, the new "Take the Train to the Game" promotion allows attendees of Mets home games to receive $5 off certain LIRR tickets, good for use on gameday. The discount applies for day passes or CityTicket day passes to Mets-Willets Point purchased through the TrainTime app. Get more information on the deal here. Public transportation to Citi Field Subway: For $3, take the 7 train to Mets-Willets Point and follow the signs to Citi Field. There is an accessible exit on the Flushing-bound platform that remains open on game days. The MTA will operate additional and express trains on game days "as frequently as possible." Bus: Also for $3, take the Q90 bus to Seaver Way. Bulgogi beef cheesesteak spring roll, anyone? Too many words to fit in your mouth? How about: burger. Citi Field is known for its creative food options, and the stadium is upping the ante again for the 2026 season. More than three dozen new food items are being introduced, with wings, empanadas, and not-your-average burgers all making the list. Sure, hot dogs and pizza will be on the menu, too, along with loaded cornbread, a chopped cheese patty, and Brooklyn native Adam Richman's Burger Hall. The day could be a home run both on the field and in the stands, because the weather should work out beautifully. First pitch temperature will be near 70 degrees, above normal for this time of year. We may get a few peeks of sunshine early in the afternoon, too, which will brighten the day for everyone involved. For players, a brisk south wind at 15 mph – with gusts over 20 mph at times – could be heaven for hitters. At Citi Field, a south wind blows from home plate into center field. That means hitters will have a tailwind that could help take their fly balls the distance. Who wouldn’t love a little home run derby to start the season? The Pirates also put out their starting lineup, though the biggest name for Pittsburgh won't be in the batter's box — he's on the mound. Paul Skenes will get the start for the Pirates, as the defending NL Cy Young Award winner looks to continue the incredible start he's had to his career (he's still just 23 years old). Here's a look at the starting lineup for Pittsburgh: Oneil Cruz (CF) Brandon Lowe (2B) Bryan Reynolds (LF) Marcell Ozuna (DH) Ryan O'Hearn (RF) Jared Triolo (SS) Spencer Horwitz (1B) Nick Gonzales (3B) Henry Davis (C) Francisco Lindor is batting leadoff for the Mets as they kick off their 2026 season. Juan Soto will be behind him, followed by Bo Bichette and Jorge Polanco. Newly acquired Freddy Peralta will be taking the mound for the Amazins. Here's a look at the starting lineup: Francisco Lindor (SS) Juan Soto (LF) Bo Bichette (3B) Jorge Polanco (1B) Luis Robert Jr. (CF) Brett Baty (DH) Marcus Semien (2B) Carson Benge (RF) Francisco Alvarez (C)3 TODAY's Al Roker donned a Mets jersey for Opening Day! The team shared a photo of the meteorologist alongside Mr. and Mrs. Met. There are plenty of familiar faces (Francisco Lindor, Juan Soto, Brett Baty) along with more than a few new names for the Mets this season, including new players signed or traded for (Marcus Semien, Devin Williams) and at least one rookie looking to make a name for himself (Carson Benge). Benge is a name some fans may not be familiar with. The rookie used a stellar Spring Training to make the team and looks to be the team's starting right fielder (with Soto moving to left field). One name not on the list is a nine-time All-Star reliever who did not make the team out of camp — but it appears he may stick with the franchise. Former closer Craig Kimbrel — fifth all-time in saves with 440 — was not on the Opening Day roster.
